text:
Tampa Bay comes in 3-0-2 over its last five, riding a 4-1 win over a Chicago team that has now gone winless in five. Minnesota is on the second night of a back-to-back, having beaten San Jose 4-1 last night for its third straight win. The Wild are without Nick Foligno, Marcus Foligno and Jared Spurgeon, and they lost the chance battle in four of their last five, so the streak leans on goaltending more than chances. TBL won the October meeting 3-2.

On the numbers, there's little between them. At five on five, TBL has taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games and MIN 54%. Minnesota's power play creates more (0.97 expected goals per game to 0.76), and its penalty kill gives up a bit more (0.63 to 0.54). In net, both backups are projected: Dennis Hildeby for TBL, at -0.18 goals saved above expected this season (a measure of how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shot quality predicts), and Calvin Pickard for MIN, at -2.27. Hildeby was at +10.06 over 20 games last year, Pickard at -3.54 over 16.

Kirill Kaprizov is on a seven-game point streak and has a 47% chance to score, our highest on the night. Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek are on seven-game streaks too. For Tampa Bay, Brayden Point is one point shy of 700 for his career, and Brandon Hagel has the Lightning's best goal probability at 39%.
